stem.en: A solid compound does not conduct electricity, but its solution in water conducts well. What does this tell you about the compound?

text.en: It is ionic: it already contains ions, which are fixed in the solid and free in the solution.
It is covalent: dissolving in water always makes ions from covalent compounds.
It is a metal, because only metals conduct electricity.

explanation.en: Dissolving sets free ions that are already there, so the solid must contain ions that were held in place. This is an ionic compound. Option b does not fit sugar, which is covalent and gives no ions when it dissolves. Option c does not fit either: a metal conducts as a solid, and salt water conducts although salt is not a metal.

hints.en: The solution conducts, so ions are moving in it. Were they made by the water, or were they in the solid already?
